Insurgency -- A source mod turned stand-alone game developed by New World Interactive.

I'll start up front by saying that I never played this while it was just a mod, I've only placed since it's stand-alone release.

If you're looking for a good game to play co-op with friends, or a competitive multiplayer fps look no further -- However, if you're looking for the Call of Duty style run-and-gun, halo jumping "arcade" style action this may not be for you.

It is, as defined by it's user tags on steam, a more tactical and realistic style of FPS -- for example, a shot to centre mass of your enemy will mostly likely result in a kill with any high caliber weapon, and 1-2 shots in centre mass with any other low caliber weapon is also a kill. There is no dumping 9 rounds into someone and hoping they're dead.

However, at the same time, it's not realistic to the point of having bullet drop.. the ballistics are nice and there are quite a few sound mods that increase the immersiveness as well as re-textures for weapons available from the Steam Workshop. It's also fair to say that there is a plethura of custom maps for both co-op and multiplayer game modes.

TL:DR -- A great co-op game for playing with a few mates, decent ballistics, immersive sounds.. A great game for players who enjoy tactical gameplay more then arcade style'd games.

Quando comprei quis reembolso na primeira semana. Hoje é o FPS que eu mais jogo. E sou ruim demais, basta ver meus stats. Insurgency é tenso, tenso demais. Tenso num jeito que muito jogo de terror psicológico por ai luta pra tentar ser.

As balas voando do seu lado e estourando na parede, os gritos dos companheiros de time, os gritos do seu próprio char. Tudo contribui pra atmosfera pesada do jogo, talvez um dos simuladores mais realistas de combate em ambientes fechados típicos das insurgências e das guerras de guerrilha. Cada esquina é um perigo, rushar é se tornar um alvo ambulante... gruda no teu time e vai com Deus. E esse é outro aspecto sensacional desse jogo: a dependência do co-op e de jogar bem em time.

A comunidade é sensacional, pouco tóxica (como as de CS:GO, por exemplo). Dou muita risada no chat aberto entre os rounds e é sempre mais engraçado quando um argentino entra.

Eu recomendo demais esse jogo! Mais do que o Sandstorm que mal tem servers BR.

imo, Insurgency and it's sequel are among the best tactical shooters out there. They have a nice mix of arcade action and tactical mechanics, the weapon handling is the best-feeling of any game I've ever played, and the sound design is simply the most impressive I've heard from any game made on the Source engine (with the excellent Resistance and Liberation coming in a surprisingly distant second).

This particular mixture of one-or-two shot kills and a fast-enough round 'n' wave-based game structure are a fantastic cocktail; like a combo of Counter Strike's arcade-like pacing 'n' style of gameplay, with a bit of the tactical, crawling tension of games like Red Orchestra and ARMA. These games and Day of Infamy do just enough to fully differentiate themselves from virtually everything else on the market right now (at least, that I'm aware of). Absolutely cannot recommend them enough.

The gunplay and general 'realism' of this game are superior to the sequel, Sandstorm, in pretty much every way. Overall I enjoy this game more, but I can't deny Sandstorm is also very fun and has its own appeals. For the more hardcore tactical FPS players, the OG game here is the one you want. Amazing title, can't recommend it enough.. though these days the community isn't too huge I will forewarn. That said, I still recommend you buy Sandstorm too, as both are great games that have their own appeals.

Insurgency has no flaws. Even to a pessimist.
This challenging shooter is smart, rewarding and, most importantly, utterly impressive. The gameplay design choice to remove most of the HUD and the entire kill feedback altogether was ingenious.
The decision to add the non-zoomed background when looking through the scope, material penetration, a great sound library (Even the non-integral feature of the game the Alackhu Akbar mod that I can't play without) and all the other small details that we will never notice make up the crown jewel of Insurgency.
Oh, and the devs are just great, since they have created good free content. Lots of it. They're really far from the greediness of Overkill and sometimes seem more productive than the devs on Rust.

There's no doubt - Insurgency is very realistic. But not barely playable hyper-realistic. For me it took about 5-6 games of being absolutely useless to get used to it and to get my bearings for it. Afterward, I felt well adapted to the system because it was pretty easy to learn. I enjoy the class selection and customization and many various options allowed for each class and team. The game itself runs smooth, has excellent mechanics, and offers you more than just one thing to do than shoot everything in sight; it requires you to do more than that. The bots mode, which is a mode that should be on almost every 1st person shooter in my opinion, is very useful for practice and if you don't want to have to fight humans all the time. The developers seem quite dedicated to their product and add content to their game for no extra cost, even though they easily could. This game is equally playable by yourself or with friends (Although every game is better with friends, right?) and there's a nice bundle available if you're the giving type. Overall, this game may not be for everyone, but considering its exceptionally low price for a massive amount of content, good guy Greg developers, and mecanics that were paid attention to, it is a great buy.

Hard to say tho. If you wanna find a new experience with more tactical FPS game, this would be for you. The gun play is kinda simple with every almost recoil can be compensated with dragging the mouse down, but the AI is horrendously terrifying for their able to just spawn behind you, much like L4D series with the Hunters, Smokers cheesy placement which is a trait that shares between old games and older (unnatural spawnings).

Personally, i found this game very useful for aim practice, especially in Survival mode or Outpost so please do keep it in mind.

The servers are also the spotlight in this game which fortunately provide varied kinda experience from got blown up in the face with the kamikaze C4 man, sniped by an LMG from 400 KMs away to use white phosphorus in the battlefield. It's great.

Most importantly, only play this game if you can: a) speak english b) read english c) use more than 3 braincells to think.

This game is a favorite of mine from my more formative years, and while I believe this game has many qualities that puts it above it's younger brother, Sandstorm, I cannot in good faith recommend anyone purchase this game in current year.

What few servers remain populated are pretty much only EU based, which is plagued by boot-sucking fascist edge-lords who spam racial slurs, and if you're based in anywhere other than western Europe, also bad ping.

The only game mode that is still populated is Rush, which is odd because it sort of represents the antithesis of the gameplay Insurgency is trying to achieve with slower paced tactical engagements, trading that for twitchy paranoid frantic shooting around corners and little time to strategize with your team.

I wouldn't mind playing more Insurgency Sandstorm, but it's just not the same. Save your money and just get Sandstorm.
